newsitem.title: USA: BP Texas methanol plant up, force majeure remains.
newsitem.headline: BP Texas methanol plant up, force majeure remains.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc unit BP Chemicals said Tuesday it has restarted its 10,000 barrel per day jointly-operated methanol plant in Texas City but all of the output is still in force majeure.
"I expect to be in force majeure for the rest of March because I need the flexibility to schedule customer pickups," said methanol business manager Bob Niedzielski.
Niedzielski said the plant restarted over the weekend after shutting down Feb 27 to fix a compressor.
"The plant is running smoothly and we are pretty much at 100 percent capacity," Niedzielki said, adding the company plans to meet all of its customer requirements.
Late last week, BP Chemical took delivery of 20,000 barrels of product into its system to help meet its commitments.
Since news of the restart, spot methanol prices by Tuesday had retraced to 60.50 cents after reaching as high as 85.00 cents, traders said.
The plant, which began production in May 1995, is a joint venture with Sterling Chemicals Inc. ((--Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631))
